title: UOS agent user policy
description: The user-adjustable policy of the AI control layer (section 5.3). The user can make the assistant stricter, and can relax the class 2 handling of accessibility and screen actions for a named application. Nothing in this file can relax class 3 or class 4. Terminal emulators and run dialogs are sensitive, and password managers are excluded, whatever this file says; nothing in it removes an entry from those built-in lists. The loader in services/uos-agent is authoritative. It also enforces rules this schema cannot express: an application has at most one relaxation, ignoring letter case and a trailing .desktop; an integer is written without a fraction or an exponent; and no field is given twice.

application.description: An application identifier: 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters, with no space at either end. An identifier with any other character could look like a listed one without being equal to it.

mode.description: normal: the rules of the design, unchanged. ask_every_action: ask before every action of every class; an unattended task is deferred. observe_only: only class 0 actions are available.

excluded_applications.description: Applications the assistant must neither observe nor act in, in addition to the built-in list. Matched without regard to ASCII case or a trailing .desktop.

sensitive_applications.description: Applications in which every accessibility and screen action, observation included, is treated as class 2 at least, in addition to the built-in list. Matched without regard to ASCII case or a trailing .desktop. Overrides a relaxation.

relaxations.description: Per-application relaxations. Each applies to accessibility and screen actions in that application only, in normal mode, while the user is present, in a window known to belong to the user, and not to an action the model itself flagged as consequential.

class.description: The class the relaxation covers. Only class 2 can be relaxed: consequential accessibility and screen actions in the application run without asking.
